function: Non-linear symbol-level precoding for downlink massive MIMO with coarse DACs: the GNN maps channel and symbol vector to quantized precoded output levels, maximizing sum rate (pp. 4-5, 8).
system: Downlink massive MIMO: 32-antenna BS, 1 to 6 single-antenna users, 1 to 4 bit DACs; 3.5 GHz carrier in power analysis; no RIS (pp. 3, 9, 12).
method: Graph neural network over antenna and user nodes (4 hidden layers, 128 features), self-supervised training maximizing sum rate via straight-through Gumbel-softmax; Adam, 200,000 channels (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. Rayleigh channels CN(0,1), 200,000 for training and 10,000 for testing; pure LOS ULA channel only for radiation patterns (pp. 5, 9).
test_conditions: Trained at 20 dB SNR, tested from -30 to 30 dB on 10,000 independent channels; M, K, and bits varied, no cross-setting test stated (pp. 9-10).
baselines: Non-learned only: MRT (single user) and ZF (multi-user) linear precoding followed by quantization, with 1-4 bit and ideal DACs; no earlier learned precoder compared (pp. 9-12).
metrics: Achievable sum rate versus SNR, bits, and users (Figs. 7, 11); symbol NMSE (Table I); radiation patterns and SDR; DAC and GNN power consumption (Figs. 12-13) (pp. 9-13).
complexity: FLOP counts derived analytically for the GNN, scaling as O(dh^2 MK + 2^b MK dh + 2^2b M); 12 TFLOPs/s needed at 1 MHz; accelerator-based power estimate (pp. 9, 12).
openness: none; no link or DOI to code or data, only third-party references.
q1_support: p. 9: "The channels are sampled from a complex normal distribution". I.i.d. Rayleigh fading, plus a pure LOS ULA channel for the radiation patterns (p. 5); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "During training, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is fixed at" 20 dB, then tested over an SNR sweep (Fig. 7). No unseen M, K, or bit setting is reported; fine-tuning on measured data is only discussed as future work (p. 13).
q3_support: p. 10: "the proposed method outperforms classical MRT precoding for one to four bits". The only baselines are MRT and ZF linear precoders (Figs. 7, 11); no earlier learned precoder is compared, and the larger GNN (dh = 256) is a variant of the proposed method.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the proposed GNN is computed in terms of real floating point operations (FLOPs)". Section V gives multiplication and addition counts and an order O(dh^2 MK + 2^b MK dh + 2^2b M).
q5_support: p. 9: "The channels are sampled from a complex normal distribution". The channels are generated by the authors; no link or DOI for code or data appears in the paper, and the cited URLs are third-party references.
notes: Included as area 3: the learned GNN is the BS precoder (non-linear, quantization-aware). The DAC power motivation is not treated as the excluded hardware function because the output is the precoded vector that maximizes the sum rate; reviewer to confirm. q3 is 0 because only MRT and ZF are compared. q4 counts the analytic FLOP count of Section V (p. 9).
